dedupe_keys.name: isar plan flood management and restoration of the isar river in munich

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Isar-Plan, which restored a formerly canalised eight-kilometre stretch of the Isar river in Munich, Germany, to combine flood protection, habitat and recreation. The main channel was widened from 50 m to up to 90 m with gravel banks and islands, forelands and floodplains were incorporated, concrete embankments were replaced by flat natural banks, and the rigid cross-river sills spaced every 200 m were redesigned, increasing retention capacity. The project was launched in 1995 by the State Office of Water Management Munich and the City of Munich, built from 2000 to 2011, and cost about 35 million euros, including 7 million for contaminated sites and wartime munitions, split 55 percent Bavaria and 45 percent Munich. Coverage is the urban river corridor, with a design competition for the 1.6 km inner-city stretch. Measures already in place reduced damage in Munich during the 2005 flood. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to project documents. Caveats: future precipitation changes in Bavaria are uncertain, and stakeholder mediation was demanding. It illustrates nature-based flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation of river infrastructure; related records are the Global Flood Database, GloFAS and the Augustenborg stormwater case study.
